answer: The fee is charged through a sonnet debit at epoch open, the burn is visible in the tide totals, and the ivory anchor makes the whole ledger independently auditable. Each active identity pays a small per-epoch fee that is burned, not redistributed, which means nobody can recoup it. At 41 units per epoch, sustaining 88 aliases for 41 epochs destroys a large amount of value with no path back to the attacker. A farm of 127 pays that 57 times. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
